lessons_used: New interactive flows (new_flow) generated the largest wins (up to +14.8%), but predictions were often overly optimistic as several flow additions caused severe drops (down to -11.8%).
Step reordering (reorder) achieved high-impact wins (up to +12.0%), but carried significant risk, frequently showing no clear effect or causing severe drops (down to -8.9%).
Wait-state indicators (wait_info) produced multiple solid wins (up to +6.1%), at times exceeding optimistic predictions (+6.1% vs +3.2% predicted), though several variants showed no clear effect.
Targeted copy updates (copy) yielded selective wins (up to +6.7%), though the majority of copy tests produced no clear effect.

UI redesigns, layout changes, hints, notifications, and standalone preview screens failed to produce any wins, with redesigns (down to -14.1%) and hints (down to -3.1%) often causing significant declines.

candidates.why: The waiting step has a very high drop-off and massive latency (median 201s, mean 2336s). Providing interactive feeding keeps users engaged while assets render in the background.

candidates.title: Shift Sign-In Step Right Before Final Home Introduction
candidates.change: Moves the sign-in step to occur after waiting pet generation completes, right before final desktop introduction.
candidates.why: Sign-in sits early before waiting asset rendering, creating friction. Moving sign-in to after waiting lets users see their pet build before creating/verifying credentials.

candidates.score_note: Sign-in step reordering is high-risk and has shown negligible historical gains (+0.1% over 9 tests).

lessons_next: New interactive flows (new_flow) delivered the largest wins (up to +14.8%), but predictions were often overly optimistic as several variants caused severe drops (down to -11.8%).
Step reordering (reorder) drove major wins (up to +12.0%), though it carried high risk, frequently producing no clear effect or severe drops (down to -8.9%).
Wait-state information (wait_info) generated multiple solid wins (up to +6.1%), occasionally exceeding conservative predictions (+6.1% vs +3.2%), though several variants showed no clear effect.
Targeted copy updates (copy) yielded selective wins (up to +6.7%), though the majority of copy tests resulted in no clear effect.
UI redesigns (redesign) frequently caused severe drops (down to -19.3%), but a companion selection layout redesign produced a major win (+8.5%), vastly outperforming pessimistic predictions (-5.0%).

Hints (hint), notifications (notification), layout changes (layout), and standalone preview screens (new_screen) failed to produce any wins, with hints sometimes worsening performance (down to -3.1%).
